settings_updates_ahead_note: Note under the version tiles in Settings > General > Updates when the app runs a build newer than the followed channel's newest offer, so no update is offered. {channel} is the channel's display name (Stable, Beta or Alpha), {version} the version the channel offers.
settings_updates_auto_aria: Accessible name of the switch that turns the automatic update check on or off in Settings > General > Updates.
settings_updates_auto_hint: Tooltip of the automatic-check switch: when the app checks. The 6 hours match CHECK_EVERY_MS in updates.ts.
settings_updates_auto_label: Label next to the switch that turns the automatic update check on or off.
settings_updates_card_fallback_body: Body of the corner card shown once after an update when the changelog has no summary line for the new version.
settings_updates_card_see_whats_new: Button on the corner card shown once after an update; opens the What's new sheet for the version just installed.
settings_updates_card_title: Title of the corner card shown once after an update. {version} is the version now running.
settings_updates_check_failed: Title of the error alert in Settings > General > Updates when asking GitHub for the newest release failed; the reason follows as the body.
settings_updates_check_now: Button in Settings > General > Updates that asks GitHub for the newest release right away.
settings_updates_checked_at: Line under the headline of the Updates card: when the last check finished. {time} is a localized time of day, hours and minutes.
settings_updates_details_hide: Link under the install steps in Settings > General > Updates that hides the install log.
settings_updates_details_show: Link under the install steps in Settings > General > Updates that shows the install log (the output of `atlas update`).
settings_updates_dev_hot_reload: Keycap-style label before the command that starts the desktop app with hot reload, in the dev link box. Lowercase on purpose: it names an action next to a command.
settings_updates_dev_link_body: Explanation in the dev link box of Settings > General > Updates: this app or CLI is linked to a source checkout, so updates are paused.
settings_updates_dev_link_title: Title of the box that explains the app is linked to a local checkout (`atlas link --desktop`).
settings_updates_dev_rebuild: Keycap-style label before the command that rebuilds and relinks the desktop app, in the dev link box. Lowercase on purpose: it names an action next to a command.
settings_updates_downgrade_warning: Warning in the downgrade confirmation of the update channel panel: an older build may not read what a newer one wrote. ~/.atlas is the data folder and stays verbatim.
settings_updates_full_changelog: Link to the project's full changelog page, in Settings > General > Updates and in the What's new sheet. Keep changelog as the file's name.
settings_updates_github_unreachable: Shown in the What's new sheet when loading the release notes failed and the backend gave no reason (offline, no GitHub answer). The sheet has a Retry button next to it.
settings_updates_headline_checking: Headline of the Updates card while a check for a newer release runs.
settings_updates_headline_current: Headline of the Updates card when the last check found nothing newer; also the toast of a manual check or a finished install with the same result.
settings_updates_headline_dev: Headline of the Updates card when the app runs from a source checkout or a dev link, so updates are paused.
settings_updates_headline_installing: Headline of the Updates card while an install runs and the target version is not known.
settings_updates_headline_installing_to: Headline of the Updates card while an install runs. {version} is the version being installed.
settings_updates_headline_restart: Headline of the Updates card after an install: the app must restart to run the new version.
settings_updates_headline_unknown: Headline of the Updates card when no check has finished or the last one failed, so nothing is claimed about versions.
settings_updates_install_downgrade: Button that installs an older build the followed channel offers; shown in Settings > Updates and in the channel switch panel. {version} is the older version. Downgrade stays English as developers say it.
settings_updates_install_now_password: Button in the managed-install alert that lets Atlas run the package manager's command; the system then asks for the user's password.

settings_updates_log_starting.description: Placeholder in the install log before the CLI printed its first line.
settings_updates_log_starting.distinct: A log pane placeholder, not a process status; the panel uptime text with the same English word is its own screen.

settings_updates_looking_newest: Line under the headline of the Updates card while a check runs.
settings_updates_managed_by: Title when a package manager owns this install and Atlas cannot update it itself. {manager} is the manager's own name (Homebrew, apt, pacman...), never translated.
settings_updates_managed_by_package: Title when a package manager owns this install but the CLI did not name which one.
settings_updates_managed_run: Sentence before the command the user must run to update a package-managed install; the command follows on the same line.
settings_updates_notify_body: Body of the native notification sent once per new version; the title is the available headline.
settings_updates_reinstall_app: Button in Settings > General > Updates that downloads and installs the current app again from the newest release (repairs a broken install).
settings_updates_release_on_github: Link to the GitHub page of the newest release, under the headline of the Updates card.
settings_updates_restart_atlas: Button in Settings > General > Updates after an install: quits and reopens the app on the new version.
settings_updates_skipped_note: Note in Settings > General > Updates when a newer release exists but the user skipped it. {version} is the skipped version.

settings_updates_step_download.description: Label of the first install step: downloading the release archives. Keep it to one or two words, it sits in a row of six steps.
settings_updates_step_download.distinct: An install step (an infinitive in Portuguese, Baixar); the website's Download nav link is a different thing.

settings_updates_step_install_cli: Label of the install step that replaces the atlas command-line program. CLI stays English.
settings_updates_step_relaunch: Label of the last install step: the app reopens on the new version. Keep it to one or two words, it sits in a row of six steps.
settings_updates_step_update_app: Label of the install step that replaces the desktop app bundle.
settings_updates_step_verify: Label of the install step that checks the SHA-256 of the downloads. Keep it to one or two words.
settings_updates_stop_skipping: Link next to the skipped-version note that makes Atlas offer and notify that version again.
settings_updates_tag_linked: Small tag on a version tile when the CLI or app is linked to a source checkout (`atlas link`).
settings_updates_toast_available_skipped: Toast of a manual check when a newer release exists but the user skipped it. {version} is the release version.
settings_updates_toast_managed_command: Toast after the CLI declined to install because a package manager owns Atlas. {title} is the translated managed-by title, {command} the exact command, kept verbatim in backticks.
settings_updates_toast_managed_package: Toast after the CLI declined to install because a package manager owns Atlas and gave no command. `atlas update` stays verbatim.
settings_updates_toast_skipped: Toast after the user chose Skip this version in What's new. {version} is the skipped version.
settings_updates_toast_unlinked: Toast after the dev link was removed and the app and CLI run the published release again.
settings_updates_unlink_dev: Button in Settings > General > Updates that removes the dev link and goes back to the published release build.
settings_updates_update_all: Button in Settings > General > Updates that installs the newer CLI and desktop app.
settings_updates_updating: Label of the update buttons (Settings and What's new) while the install runs.
settings_updates_withdrawn_older: Second sentence of the withdrawn notice when the channel's newest safe release is older than what runs: nothing to update to, the explicit install button does it.
settings_updates_withdrawn_replacement: Sentence of the withdrawn notice naming the version that replaces it. {replacement} is that version.
settings_updates_withdrawn_title: Title of the warning shown when the running version was withdrawn (yanked) for a defect.
settings_updates_withdrawn_update: Sentence of the withdrawn notice when an update is on offer: installing it gets the user off the withdrawn version.
